headline: Boating Hire and Navigation Safety Guidelines
reservation: Access to the waterways is free for public use, but hiring private cruisers or day boats requires advanced booking through independent boatyards. All boaters must review the Broads Authority's water safety and navigation rules before departing to protect the fragile wetland environment.

days.title: Northern Broads Exploration

stops.name: Bure Valley Waterways
stops.detail: Navigate the heart of the northern rivers through the charming village of Horning.

stops.name: Hoveton Visitor Centre
stops.detail: Gather essential safety information and wildlife guides for identifying rare Swallowtail butterflies.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local road travel or 3 hours by boat; conditions vary
days.note: The Bure can be busy; unhurried boating is recommended to maintain the park's tranquil character.

days.title: Heritage and Windmills

stops.name: Horsey Mill
stops.detail: Visit this iconic drainage windpump, a landmark of the region's historic peat-working landscape.

stops.name: Hickling Broad
stops.detail: Explore the largest broad in the park, a vital habitat for internationally protected dragonflies.

days.note: Some broads have seasonal navigation restrictions in autumn; check current authority notices.

days.title: Southern Broads Tranquility

stops.name: River Waveney
stops.detail: Experience the quieter, intimate beauty of the Suffolk Broads winding through ancient marshes.

stops.name: St Benets Abbey
stops.detail: Walk through the ruins of this historic site that once participated in the medieval peat trade.

days.note: The southern region offers a softer, less crowded treasure for contemplative walks.

intel.title: Waterside Staithes
intel.text: Parking is available at village staithes like Loddon and Ranworth for those arriving by car. Spaces serve as launch points for both boaters and hikers along riverside paths.

intel.title: Navigational Apps
intel.text: A digital visitor app is available for navigation, but physical maps are recommended as backups on the water. Signal can be weak in the remote reed beds of the northern fens.

intel.title: Boat Fuel and Supplies
intel.text: Boatyards in Wroxham, Potter Heigham, and Oulton Broad provide fuel and pump-out services. Local riverside pubs are the primary source for food and supplies in the interior.

intel.title: Pace of Life
intel.text: The park is designed for 'slow adventure' with strict speed limits on all 125 miles of navigable waterways. Allow ample time for mooring, especially at popular staithes during mid-day.

intel.title: Accessible Boating
intel.text: The Nancy Oldfield Trust provides sailing opportunities on Barton Broad for those with disabilities. Many visitor centres and paths are designed for level access to the water's edge.

plan.arrival: Arrive via rail to Norwich or Great Yarmouth, then take local bus or transfer to a riverside boatyard for check-in.
plan.vehicle: Cruiser boats are the primary mode of travel; for land-based visitors, cars are suitable for reaching remote mills.
plan.goldenHour: Horsey Mill is a named viewpoint for sunset photography over the winding waterways.
